newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps tentatively firm, fuel climbs $2.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps tentatively firm, fuel climbs $2.

text.p: European oil swaps climbed tentatively higher on Wednesday but most markets were slow and some dealers remain sceptical of recent gains.
"Its was just a catch-up with crude," said a fuel trader explaining gains of $2 a tonne.
May barges talked around $83.50 with low sulphur around $3 higher but activity was thin. June barges stayed about 50 cents higher with July a further 75 cents above June.
Low sulphur traded at $87 in May but talked nearer $99 in the fourth quarter.
Some dealers expected prices to stay under pressure due to recent high refinery runs and expectations of higher Russian exports.
The spring thaw in Russia has unlocked frozen rivers and fuel has begun flowing from the key outlet of St Petersburg.
Brent CFDs edged a couple of cents higher for next week after physical cargoes traded at 27 cents under June compared to 29 under on Tuesday.
Next week's CFDs talked 28 cents under June and traded flat a couple of time against the following week of 12-16 May.
Monthly CFDs remain in contango with May and June valued around 30 cents under the front line IPE Brent and 23 cents under respectively.
The third and fourth quarters were 14 cents and 12 cents under respectively with the whole of 1998 talking either side of five cents under the screen.
Gasoline talked around $199 for May about $2 above the $196 that talked for much of Tuesday.
He pegged gasoline crack spreads little changed at $5.25 a barrel for May, $4.05 for the third quarter and $3.10 for the fourth quarter.
There were mixed signals on gasoline stocks in the U.S. but traders report at least two cargoes of cat gas have moved transatlantic in recent weeks.
Middle distillates were little changed. Gas oil crack spreads against Brent talked $4.30 a barrel (3Q97), $4.85 (4Q97), $4.75 (1Q98), $4.10 (2Q98).
Swaps for physical gas oil cargoes held at $6 a tonne and $14.75 over the IPE for May 0.2 and EN590 respectively.
Jet premiums above the IPE also held steady. May was pegged around $24.50 a tonne over while June was $25.00 over.
